sections.html:
Smyrna, in Rutherford County and part of the Nashville metro area, had an estimated 63,321 residents on July 1, 2025, which is 19.2% more than the 2020 base. The median value of an owner's home is $358,300 and owners live in 57.4% of homes. Renters pay a median $1,461.

Households average 2.79 people, which points to a market of families, so lead a listing with bedroom count and yard space.

Smyrna taxpayers get a single bill from the Rutherford County Trustee that combines the town and county levies. The Trustee has collected both together since October 2017.

2025 Smyrna property tax rates
Levy2025 rate per $100 assessed
Rutherford County$1.8762
Town of Smyrna$0.5257
Combined$2.4019

Houses are assessed at 25% of value. Your 2026 bill may carry a different rate, so read it for the figure that was actually applied.

sections.h2: Due dates and who pays at closing
sections.html:
The bill comes due on the first Monday of October and can be paid interest-free into late February. There is no early-payment discount. Taxes cover January 1 through December 31, so a mid-year sale divides the bill by months owned.

A new owner should check the closing statement or ask the title company who pays, since unpaid tax stays on the parcel. When a lender escrows your tax, the bill you receive is informational. You can pay at the Smyrna office, in Murfreesboro, online or by mail. The Smyrna counter is at 615-898-7705.

The Comptroller's 2026 list shows a $54,690 standard freeze income limit for Rutherford County. Smyrna uses the higher $63,470 local option. Filing closes 35 days after the delinquency date, in April.

A freeze holds the tax at the first approved year's amount, so a seller with one should alert the title company. To dispute a value, the county Board of Equalization sits from June 1. A further appeal to the state board is due August 1 or 45 days after the county board's notice, whichever comes later.

Smyrna's zoning ordinance bars renting a single detached dwelling, or any part of it, for less than three months. Once a tenant has stayed three months or more, later extensions can be shorter. The town may ask for the lease or agreement and can cite a violation after notice. A buyer who plans nightly stays will not find that route open.

Repairs have their own rule. Homeowner permits are issued only where the owner lives, or plans to live, in the house. They are not issued when the work is for resale or lease, so sale prep needs a contractor with a state license to pull the permit. The Building Safety Department at 315 S. Lowry Street handles permits, and additions or decks begin with a site plan sent to permits@townofsmyrna.org.

  • Interior remodels start with a pre-permit inspection, 615-355-5704.
  • Contractors need a state license, insurance proof and a town business tax license or release form.
  • A Certificate of Occupancy shows a structure passed inspection.

The Town Planner serves as Floodplain Administrator, and the town posts FEMA flood map panels revised May 9, 2023. Zones starting with A or V are the high-risk areas, and a federally backed mortgage on such a property requires flood insurance. Zones B, C and X carry lower but real risk.

If your house sits near Stones River, Stewarts Creek or the lake shoreline, look up the panel before you list and have the zone ready for buyers. Any work in a floodplain needs a development permit from the Floodplain Administrator, (615) 355-5706, before it starts.

Rutherford County's register charges $5 a page, $10 at minimum, plus $2 for the computer fund. The state's conveyance tax adds $3.70 per $1,000 of price. Each deed has to carry the preparer's name and address. A title company normally handles filing, and the sale agreement decides which party pays the tax.

sections.h2: Two governments, two sets of questions
sections.html: Town Hall is at 315 S. Lowry Street, which is also where permit applications are accepted in person. Ask the town about permits, zoning and flood maps. Ask the Rutherford County Trustee, Assessor or Register of Deeds about the tax bill, the appraised value and the recorded deed.

• The most recent county tax bill, which also covers the town levy.
  • Your deed, with the preparer's name and address.
  • Permit records and Certificates of Occupancy for any additions or decks.
  • The flood zone for your panel, if the house sits near the creek, river or lake.
  • Lease or rental agreement details, if a tenant lives there.
  • A mortgage payoff figure.

Smyrna sellers deal with the town and the county at once, so a short folder with these items keeps both offices answering the same questions the same way.

1. You accept an offer and a title company opens a file.
  2. The title company asks the Trustee for tax status, checks for any town maintenance lien and confirms the flood zone.
  3. The deed is signed and filed with the Rutherford County register, with the preparer's name and address on it.
  4. The conveyance tax and recording fees are paid as the sale agreement directs.
  5. The year's tax is divided by months owned, and any balance comes from your proceeds.

None of this depends on a lender when the buyer pays cash, so the date follows the title work and your own moving plans, not a bank's schedule.

Owners live in 57.4% of Smyrna homes, so a lot of houses here are rentals. A tenant who has stayed three months or more is allowed later shorter extensions, and the town may ask to see the lease. If you sell with a tenant in place, give the buyer the lease, the rent and the end date. A buyer who wants nightly stays should know the zoning ordinance rules that out.

Listing suits a house that is ready to show. When a house needs work, has a tenant or faces a deadline, an as-is cash offer can close once title is clear, with no lender approval to wait on. Put the figure in writing and compare it with what a listing would net after commission, repairs and holding costs.

Whichever way you go, get a mortgage payoff figure, ask the town whether a property maintenance lien is open, and time the closing to your move so you are not carrying two homes.

faqs.q: Does a Smyrna seller get one tax bill or two?
faqs.a: One. The Rutherford County Trustee has collected the Town of Smyrna tax together with the county tax since October 2017, so a single bill covers both.

faqs.q: What is the Smyrna town property tax rate?
faqs.a: $0.5257 per $100 assessed for 2025, added to the county's $1.8762. Your latest bill shows the 2026 rates.

faqs.q: Can I rent my Smyrna house by the night?
faqs.a: Not under the current zoning ordinance, which bars renting a single detached dwelling to any tenant for under three months.

faqs.q: Can I pull a homeowner permit to fix up a house I am selling?
faqs.a: No. A homeowner permit is only for owners who live or plan to live in the house. Work done to resell it needs a contractor with a state license to pull the permit.

faqs.q: Where do I get a flood zone answer for a Smyrna house?
faqs.a: Call the Town Planner at (615) 355-5706 or look up the FEMA panels on the town's site. Zone A or V property with a federally backed loan needs flood insurance.
